title: Local and service Google Ads: city pages that convert calls
primaryKeyword: Google Ads for small businesses in India
metaDescription: Local and service Google Ads: city pages that convert calls — Altmash's practical guide with steps, mistakes to avoid, key metrics and a 30-day plan.
keywords: Google Ads for small businesses in India
intro: Local and service Google Ads: city pages that convert calls is a question I hear from local businesses and ecommerce brands that want high-intent leads almost every week. I am Altmash — I started freelancing in 2020, opened my branding and marketing agency in 2021 and launched a clothing brand in 2023 — and the pattern is always the same: the brands that win treat Google Ads as a system, not a one-off task.
Below I walk through why it matters, a step-by-step process, the mistakes I see most often, what to measure and a practical 30-day plan you can start this week.
takeaways: Keyword, ad and landing page must answer the same question.
Profitable Search first, Performance Max later.
Report brand and non-brand results separately.
Review search terms and add negatives weekly.

sections.heading: Why Google Ads deserves a real system
paragraphs: Google Ads catches people at the exact moment they search for what you sell. That intent is valuable, but only when the keyword, the ad and the landing page all answer the same question.
Budgets leak quietly on Google: broad match without negatives, Performance Max fed with weak assets, and landing pages that load slowly on mobile data.
That is why I never start with tactics. I start by asking what the business needs from Google Ads in the next 90 days, and then build only what serves that goal.

sections.heading: Where most brands go wrong with Google Ads
paragraphs: These are the mistakes I see most often when I audit brands. Each one looks small on its own; together they explain why results stall.
If you recognise two or more of these in your own business, fix them before adding budget. More spend on a broken system only makes the problem more expensive.
bullets: Running broad match with no negative keyword list.
Sending every ad to the homepage.
Counting page views or button clicks as conversions.
Starting with Performance Max before Search has shown what converts.
Ignoring mobile page speed on Indian networks.

sections.heading: How to approach Google Ads, step by step
paragraphs: Here is the process I follow. The order matters: each step removes a reason for the next one to fail.
Do not skip the early steps to get to the exciting part. In my experience, most Google Ads problems that look like execution issues are really decisions that were never made at the start.
bullets: Map intent: group keywords into brand, product, problem and competitor themes.
Build tight campaigns: one theme per ad group, with ads that repeat the searcher's own language.
Match landing pages: send each theme to a page that answers that exact query above the fold.
Add negatives weekly: review the search terms report and block irrelevant queries.
Track real conversions: calls, WhatsApp clicks, form fills and purchases, imported with values.
Layer Performance Max carefully: only after Search is profitable and your assets and feed are clean.

sections.heading: How much time and money Google Ads takes
paragraphs: Local service businesses in India often start Google Search with ₹500 to ₹2,000 a day, while ecommerce brands usually need more for Shopping and Performance Max. Treat the first three to four weeks as a learning period spent refining keywords and negatives.

These ranges are starting points, not quotes. The right number depends on your category, your margins and how much of the work your team can handle in-house. What matters most is committing to a test long enough to learn from it.

sections.heading: Lessons from brands I have worked on
paragraphs: One example from my own work: An interior studio’s website looked premium but leaked leads — a simpler brief form plus WhatsApp routing doubled qualified conversations.
For Google Ads, the takeaway is to treat proof and clarity as part of the work, not as decoration on top of it.
Another: A founder’s personal brand started converting inbound only after content showed process and receipts — not motivational quotes.
The details differ by category, but the principle holds: when the brand, the page and the channel tell one story, Google Ads becomes cheaper and more predictable.

sections.heading: What you need in place before you start
paragraphs: You do not need expensive software to do this well. This is the stack I usually start with:
Tools only help when someone owns them. Assign one person to each tool, document the setup, and keep every login in the brand's name rather than a freelancer's personal account.
bullets: Google Ads with Google Tag or Google Tag Manager
Google Merchant Center for ecommerce feeds
Google Search Console for organic query overlap
PageSpeed Insights for landing page speed
Looker Studio for a weekly report

sections.heading: The Indian market context
paragraphs: In India, trust is often built in the chat window. A buyer who messages you on WhatsApp is judging your speed, tone and clarity as much as your product, so Google Ads has to include how your team responds.
At the same time, trust is local while expectations are global. A buyer in Jaipur or Lucknow compares your experience with the best apps on their phone, so the bar for clarity and speed keeps rising.

sections.heading: A 30-day plan you can start this week
paragraphs: If you want to move quickly, here is how I would sequence the first month.
At the end of the month you will have real data instead of opinions — and a clear picture of where to invest next.
bullets: Week 1: Map intent and build tight campaigns.
Week 2: Match landing pages.
Week 3: Add negatives weekly and track real conversions.
Week 4: Layer Performance Max carefully, then review your metrics and decide what to keep.

conclusion: The brands that get Google Ads right are rarely the ones with the biggest budgets. They are the ones with clear decisions, a weekly rhythm and someone who owns the result. Put those three in place and the rest becomes much easier.
If you want help applying this to your brand, message me on WhatsApp. I am Altmash, and I build and run brands end to end — website, identity, ads and the systems that keep them growing.

faq.q: Is Google Ads better than Meta ads?
faq.a: They do different jobs. Google captures people already searching, while Meta creates demand among people who were not searching yet. Many brands use Google for high-intent sales and Meta for discovery and retargeting.

faq.q: What is a good conversion rate for Google Ads?
faq.a: It depends heavily on industry and offer. Instead of chasing a benchmark, compare landing pages and ad groups inside your own account and keep improving the weakest ones.
Use it once Search campaigns convert and your tracking, product feed and creative assets are clean. Performance Max amplifies whatever you give it, including the problems.

faq.q: Does Altmash work with brands outside India?
faq.a: Yes. Altmash works with Indian and international brands on branding, websites, Shopify, ads and full brand management, usually coordinated over WhatsApp and video calls.

faq.q: What is the first thing to fix in Google Ads?
faq.a: Start with clarity: who it is for, what the offer is and what action you want next. Most Google Ads problems that look technical are really unclear decisions made earlier.
